Curative

KYOOR-uh-tiv · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Curative is able to cure or heal an illness.

Long before modern medicine, travelers soaked in the region's hot springs, convinced of their curative effects on aching joints.

Worked Example

The pharmaceutical company's advertisements implied the new supplement had curative effects, despite offering no real clinical evidence.

Curative specifically describes the power to heal or cure -- distinguishing real medicine from things that merely claim to heal.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

restorative: helping to restore health or strength

remedial: intended to correct or improve something, especially health

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

damaging: causing harm

unhealthful: bad for one's health

Where it sits · how much healing power it has — soothing → curative → miraculous

soothing vs. curative: Soothing means providing gentle comfort or relief without necessarily curing anything, milder than curative.

miraculous vs. curative: Miraculous means seemingly impossible in its healing power, an even stronger claim than curative.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — cur-

root — cur-: to take care of, to heal (Latin curare)

suffix — -ative

suffix — -ative: tending to (Latin -ativus)

Put it together

Put it together: Curative comes from Latin curare ('to take care of, to heal') + -ative ('tending to') -- literally 'tending to heal.'

Use the root in a new word: cure

Use the root in a new word: cure: Scientists have spent decades searching for a cure for the disease.
